name: Timeline for Repainting a Furnished 3-Bedroom Home One Room at a Time

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic timeline for a full interior repaint of a furnished 3-bedroom Los Angeles home when you can only move one room at a time?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic timeline for a full interior repaint of a furnished 3-bedroom Los Angeles home when you can only move one room at a time?

acceptedAnswer.text: When your Los Angeles home is fully furnished and you can only clear one room at a time, a full interior repaint takes longer than an empty-property project. For an average 3-bedroom, 2-bath home, expect roughly 5–9 working days with a two- to three-person crew. Day one is often spent on protection: covering flooring, moving furniture away from walls, and plastic-wrapping items in the first room. Each additional room requires similar staging time. Prep—patching nail holes, repairing minor cracks, caulking gaps, and sanding glossy areas—can add a half to full day depending on wall condition and previous paint quality. Color changes from dark to light or from strong hues to neutrals may require an extra coat, stretching the schedule. Drying times are influenced by Los Angeles microclimates; coastal areas may have more humidity, while inland areas dry faster but can require earlier start times to avoid extreme heat. Coordinating access to closets, kitchens, and bathrooms also adds complexity, so discuss priorities up front. A good contractor will phase rooms to keep at least one bedroom and main living area usable, communicate a daily plan, and help move larger pieces safely. Build in a buffer day for touch-ups and walkthrough corrections at the end.
